title: Chianti Classico
subtitle: The historic heart
objectives: Explain the difference between Chianti and Chianti Classico
Describe its rules and quality levels

steps.title: Two different wines
steps.body: Chianti covers a large area across Tuscany, with seven sub-zones like Rufina and Colli Senesi. Chianti Classico is a separate DOCG, the original zone between Florence and Siena, defined in 1716 by Cosimo III de' Medici. Classico must be at least 80% Sangiovese; white grapes were banned in 2006.
steps.highlight: Chianti Classico: a separate, original zone

steps.title: Quality levels
steps.body: Chianti Classico has three levels: Annata, the basic wine; Riserva, aged at least 24 months; and Gran Selezione, created in 2014, from estate-grown grapes aged at least 30 months. Since 2021, Gran Selezione needs at least 90% Sangiovese, and labels can name 11 villages, called UGAs, like Radda and Panzano.

steps.prompt: Chianti Classico's top level, created in 2014, is called ____.
steps.explanation: Gran Selezione sits above Riserva and Annata, with estate grapes and at least 30 months of ageing.

steps.title: The black rooster
steps.body: The black rooster, gallo nero, is Chianti Classico's symbol. Legend says Florence and Siena settled their border with a race: riders left at the first cockcrow. Florence's black rooster, starved, crowed early, so its rider got further. Every Chianti Classico bottle carries it on the neck.

steps.prompt: Chianti and Chianti Classico are the same DOCG.
steps.explanation: Not true. Chianti Classico is a separate DOCG, the original historic zone.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Chianti Classico is a separate DOCG, defined in 1716
It has Annata, Riserva and Gran Selezione
The black rooster marks every bottle
